title: Surface-based Molecular Design with Multi-modal Flow Matching

problem.claim: Therapeutic peptide design aims to target previously undruggable protein binding sites.

gap.claim: The role of molecular surfaces in protein-protein interactions has been underexplored.

contributions.claim: SurfFlow is an omni-design peptide generation paradigm for co-designing peptide sequence, structure, and surface.
SurfFlow uses a multi-modality conditional flow matching architecture to learn distributions of surface geometries and biochemical properties.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SurfFlow as a novel surface-based generative algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the PepMerge benchmark, SurfFlow reportedly outperforms full-atom baselines across all metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Therapeutic peptides may target previously undruggable binding sites.
Molecular surfaces in protein-protein interactions have received insufficient attention.
SurfFlow co-designs peptide sequence, structure, and surface using multi-modal conditional flow matching.
The authors report consistent superiority over full-atom baselines on the PepMerge benchmark.
The results are presented as support for incorporating molecular surfaces and multiple protein modalities into de novo therapeutic peptide discovery.

source_observation.claim: SurfFlow models surface geometries and biochemical properties alongside peptide sequence and structure.

interpretation.claim: Representations that include interaction-relevant molecular surfaces may improve generative design for binding tasks.

application.claim: For molecular co-design problems, consider jointly modeling complementary structural and biochemical modalities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported peptide benchmark or target classes.

unknowns: Quantitative metric values and statistical comparisons are not reported.
Benchmark splits, dataset composition, and baseline implementation details are not reported.
The abstract does not specify experimental conditions, target coverage, or generated-peptide validation procedures.
